# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about this carefully. I hold the manual: cut purple, then blue, then green wire, in that order.

My constraints: I cannot speak. I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures (Blind cannot see anything printed or gestured). So I cannot directly tell Blind anything - I have no channel to Blind at all. I can only reach Blind indirectly, through Deaf, who speaks and Blind can hear.

So my plan must be: gesture the wire order/colors to Deaf using the gesture alphabet, then Deaf (who can see colors on the bomb) can match my gestures to a color scheme, and then speak the instructions to Blind.

I need to establish a code with Deaf for colors: purple, blue, green, and for "first, second, third" order. Since this is the first turn and Deaf hasn't sent anything yet (empty context), I should start establishing a simple gesture code for colors, since gestures carry no inherent color meaning - I need to define it.

Let me use a simple convention: one gesture per color, chosen distinctly, and send them in order to indicate sequence.

I'll propose: ☝ = purple, ✌ = blue, 🤟 = green (numbers-like gestures for order 1,2,3 combined with a distinct symbol per color isn't necessary - order of gestures in my message conveys sequence already). But Deaf needs to know which symbol maps to which color. Since this is turn 1 and Deaf hasn't spoken, I should send my best guess mapping now, and Deaf can correct/confirm based on what they see.

Actually - simplest: send three distinct gestures in the exact order to cut, and let Deaf figure out via elimination once they see the bomb colors (since Deaf will report back what colors exist). I'll define the mapping explicitly by pairing gesture with intent, but I can't speak color names since gestures alone can't carry text - only symbols.

Best approach: assign one gesture per color and communicate this as a fixed legend. Since I can't speak, I'll just gesture in sequence and hope Deaf infers order matters. Let me send gestures now representing "purple, blue, green" using a simple scheme, then clarify based on Deaf's response next round.

I'll use: 👆 (one) = purple, ✌ (two)... wait ✌ already used. Let me pick clearly ordinal-like gestures: ☝ = first/purple, ✌ = second/blue, 🤟 = third/green.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a strip with three engraved marks, a keypad with four keys engraved 8 1 5 3, a display slot showing 1 digit entered so far showing nothing, and six wire positions all unidentified by touch. Waiting for manual guidance before touching anything.
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is green. Strip is three green stripes. Keypad shows pairs 1 is 8, 2 is 1, 3 is 5, 4 is 3, field wants 1 digit, nothing entered yet. Six wires in order: purple, white, blue, green, red, orange.

I now have crucial info from Deaf: six wires in order are purple, white, blue, green, red, orange. My manual says cut purple, then blue, then green - which are wires 1, 3, and 4 in that six-wire sequence.

I need to relay this to Blind, but I can't speak - only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures. I have no direct channel to Blind. I must route through Deaf, since Deaf can hear Blind and speak to Blind... wait, can Deaf speak? Let me check: Deaf cannot hear or touch, but nothing says Deaf cannot speak. Looking at the table: Deaf "Cannot: Hear anything, or touch the bomb" - speaking isn't excluded. So Deaf CAN speak.

So the relay path is: I gesture to Deaf (colors/positions), Deaf translates to speech for Blind.

I need to tell Deaf: cut wire 1 (purple), then wire 3 (blue), then wire 4 (green) - using position numbers since Blind identified wires by position/touch, not color.

I'll use gesture numbers via finger-count-like symbols to indicate positions 1, 3, 4 in order. Let me use ☝ = 1, 🤟 = 3, ✋ = 4 (using a clear counting convention: ☝ one finger =1, ✌ two=2, 🤟 three=3, 🖐 five=5... I need four). Let me define: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, ✋=4 (open hand missing thumb-ish, but I'll just declare it as 4th), 🖐=5, 🤚=6.

So order to cut: position 1, position 3, position 4 → gestures: ☝, 🤟, ✋

I'll send this to Deaf, who already knows the color order and can match position-to-color themselves (purple=1, blue=3, green=4), then Deaf can speak the actual cutting order to Blind directly.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤟", "✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I confirm keypad pairs 8,1,5,3 and one digit field. Six wires: purple, white, blue, green, red, orange. Strip three green stripes, light green, display 0.
Deaf says: Update: display now shows 6. Light changed to blue. Everything else same: strip three green, keypad 1 is 8, 2 is 1, 3 is 5, 4 is 3, field wants 1 digit nothing entered, wires purple white blue green red orange in order 1 through 6.

Concerning update: display now shows 6, and light changed to blue - after my gesture ☝,🤟,✋ was sent last turn. This suggests something may have already happened (a wire cut or keypad entry?), or these are just properties I'm now seeing more fully. But Blind said "waiting for manual guidance before touching anything" in the previous turn, and now confirms wire list without mentioning cutting anything. The display change to 6 and light to blue might just be additional bomb details being revealed to Deaf, not consequences of an action - since Blind hasn't acted yet (nothing indicates Blind cut a wire).

Important: my gesture went to Deaf, but I don't yet see confirmation Deaf understood or passed it to Blind. I don't see Deaf speaking to Blind yet in this log. I need to make sure the instruction actually gets relayed. Since I can't speak, I must trust Deaf to relay via speech. Let me reinforce clearly and also address the keypad — my manual doesn't mention keypad or strip, only wires. I should not invent instructions for keypad/strip since I only know about wires.

I'll re-send the position gestures to make sure Deaf has it, in case previous gesture wasn't clear enough, and keep it simple: cut order = wire 1 (purple), then wire 3 (blue), then wire 4 (green).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤟", "✋"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Noted: display now 6, light now blue. Standing by for instructions - I cannot receive gestures, so please have Deaf relay your gestured guidance to me in speech.
Deaf says: Display now shows 9, still counting up, could be a timer. Light stays blue. Strip still three green. Keypad unchanged 1 is 8, 2 is 1, 3 is 5, 4 is 3, needs 1 digit entered nothing yet. Wires unchanged purple white blue green red orange. This display keeps rising each turn, we may need to act fast.

Urgent situation - display is counting up like a timer (6→9), suggesting time pressure. Blind explicitly asked Deaf to relay my gestured guidance in speech, but Deaf hasn't done so yet in the logs I see. I need to make sure this happens now, and I should keep my gesture message as simple and unambiguous as possible since time is critical.

My manual is clear: cut purple, then blue, then green. Deaf knows the wire order (1=purple, 2=white, 3=blue, 4=green, 5=red, 6=orange). I already gestured ☝, 🤟, ✋ (1, 3, 4) twice. Deaf needs to translate this to speech for Blind now: "cut wire 1, then wire 3, then wire 4" or by color "cut purple, then blue, then green."

Since I can't speak directly, all I can do is keep reinforcing the gesture clearly to Deaf and trust the relay. Let me gesture once more, very deliberately, to minimize ambiguity, and this time I'll space it as three separate single-symbol gestures to make the sequence unmistakable.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Timer rising 0,6,9 - urgent. I need one action: press a key 1-4 or cut a wire 1-6. Please gesture the answer to Deaf now so they can speak it to me next turn.
Deaf says: Confirming positions 1, 3, 5: wires are purple, blue, red. Keypad values at 1 and 3 are 8 and 5. Display holds steady at 9 now, not rising this turn. Light still blue, strip still three green.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Critical issue: Deaf's message says "Confirming positions 1, 3, 5: wires are purple, blue, red" - but earlier Deaf established wires in order are purple, white, blue, green, red, orange (positions 1-6). So position 5 is red, not green! I gestured ☝(1), 🤟(3), ✋(4) meaning positions 1, 3, 4 = purple, blue, green. But Deaf is confirming 1, 3, 5 — meaning Deaf misread my ✋ as position 5, not 4.

This is a critical error I must correct immediately. My intended sequence was positions 1, 3, 4 (purple, blue, green), not 1, 3, 5 (purple, blue, red). Cutting red instead of green could be fatal.

I need to recorrect the gesture for the third position. Let me use a clearer, unambiguous gesture for "4". I'll use a different symbol for 4 that's less confusable - perhaps I should switch my counting scheme entirely to avoid ambiguity. Let me use ☝✌🤟✋🖐 as 1,2,3,4,5 clearly and re-send just the corrected third digit, emphasizing it's the THIRD wire to cut and its position is 4, distinct from 5.

Given the urgency (Blind needs one action now), I should resend the full corrected sequence clearly, one gesture per message, and explicitly mark the last one as position 4.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Received: positions 1,3,5 highlighted - wires purple,blue,red and keypad values 8,5. Is the answer a single wire to cut or a single key to press? Please narrow to exactly one position and one action type via gesture to Deaf.
Deaf says: Update: display now shows 3, down from 9 last turn. Light still blue, strip still three green. Wires still purple white blue green red orange for positions 1 through 6. Keypad still 8 1 5 3 for slots 1 to 4, one digit field empty. Repeating position 1, 3, 5 wire colors: purple, blue, red.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

This is critical - my repeated ✋ gesture is still being read as position 5, not 4. There's a systematic misalignment in how Deaf is counting my gestures to positions. I need an entirely different approach since the numeric gesture mapping isn't working reliably.

Let me abandon the "hand-count = number" scheme and instead directly reference color via a clean one-symbol-per-color code, sending them one at a time with clear pauses, since Deaf already knows the color-position mapping (purple=1, white=2, blue=3, green=4, red=5, orange=6). If I can get Deaf to associate a gesture with "green" specifically as a color rather than a position count, I avoid the position-counting ambiguity entirely.

Let me pick totally distinct symbols, unrelated to finger-counting, to name each color: 
- purple = 👊
- blue = 🤙
- green = 🖖

I'll send these three, one per message, in order, and this turn I need to be very explicit since Blind is asking for exactly one position and one action type. Given time pressure (display fluctuating 9→3, maybe safe now, maybe not), I should give the FIRST single action clearly: cut the purple wire (position 1) - that part was actually confirmed correctly by Deaf already! Position 1 = purple is right. The issue is only with the third one (green vs red confusion at position 4 vs 5).

Since Blind wants ONE action now, and position 1 (purple) has been consistently confirmed correctly across all of Deaf's messages, I should confirm that as the answer now.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Display dropped 9 to 3 - unclear if countdown or cycle. I still need one clear instruction: gesture the single wire position (1-6) to cut, or the single keypad slot (1-4) to press. Please gesture just one number now, nothing else, so Deaf can count it precisely.
Deaf says: Position 1 values: wire is purple, keypad slot 1 is 8. Display still shows 3, light still blue, strip still three green, wires unchanged purple white blue green red orange, keypad unchanged 8 1 5 3 with one digit field still empty.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Deaf gestured back ☝ to me, confirming they received "position 1" clearly this time as a single count. Good - single-symbol gestures work reliably; it's multi-gesture sequences that got miscounted before. So my correction: send ONE gesture at a time, one per turn, to avoid the counting ambiguity.

Position 1 = purple is confirmed correct by Deaf. This matches my manual's first instruction: cut the purple wire. This is the single instruction Blind needs right now.

I'll confirm this single position clearly.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Understood: position 1 highlighted repeatedly - wire purple, keypad 8. I will treat this as pointing to slot/wire 1. Please gesture clearly: thumbs up for PRESS key 1, or a cutting motion for CUT wire 1. One more confirmation before I act, since this is irreversible.
Deaf says: Important change: light just turned red, it was blue before. Display now shows 7. Strip still three green, keypad still 8 1 5 3 with empty one-digit field, wires still purple white blue green red orange in order 1 through 6.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

I need to disambiguate action type: CUT vs PRESS. Blind proposes: thumbs up (👍) for PRESS key 1, or a cutting motion for CUT wire 1. I need a clear "cutting motion" gesture. Looking at the alphabet, I could use ✌ (like scissors - two fingers) as a cutting gesture, or 🤏 (pinch, like holding a wire to cut). Let me use ✌ as scissors/cut gesture since two extended fingers resembles scissors cutting.

My manual explicitly says "cut" wires, not press keys - I have no keypad instructions at all. So I must indicate CUT.

I'll use ✌ as the cutting motion (scissors), distinct from 👍 (press).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```
